The stage was set for a classic cup tie on September 8, 2026, as two sides hungry for progress faced off in the Carabao Cup . With knockout football on the line, the atmosphere was electric from the opening whistle as both tactical setups looked for a decisive edge. A First Half of Near Misses Sunderland started the brighter of the two sides, looking to use the width of the pitch to stretch the Hull City defense. Early on, Wilson Isidor found himself in a promising position following a Trai Hume cross, but his effort whistled past the post. The home side continued to pile on the pressure, with Jules Ahoka forcing a fine save from Dillon Phillips . The Hull City goalkeeper was kept busy throughout the opening period, notably denying Chemsdine Talbi with a sharp stop just before the break. Hull City were not without their moments, looking dangerous on the break through the pace of Mohamed-Ali Cho . The forward sent a warning shot from distance that narrowly missed the target, but for the most part, the visitors were forced to focus on their defensive duties. Despite several corners and half-chances for the hosts, the first half concluded without a goal, leaving the tactical battle wide open for the second period. Talbi Strikes to Decide the Tie The second half saw the intensity ramp up as both managers looked to their benches for inspiration. The introduction of Thomas Meunier provided the spark Sunderland needed. In the 71st minute, a swift counter-attack saw Meunier slide a perfectly weighted through ball to Chemsdine Talbi . From outside the box, Talbi unleashed a magnificent right-footed strike that flew into the top left corner, leaving Phillips with no chance and giving the home fans reason to celebrate. Hull City threw everything forward in the closing stages, searching desperately for an equalizer. Joe Gelhardt missed a golden opportunity from close range, and a flurry of late corners kept the Sunderland faithful on the edge of their seats. However, with Omar Alderete and Luke O'Nien holding firm at the back, the hosts navigated the five minutes of added time to secure their place in the next round, surviving a late scare from a resilient Hull side.

Professional Finish to Progress To their credit, Middlesbrough refused to go down without a fight. On February 5, 2026 , two heavyweights of English football collided in a high-stakes Carabao Cup encounter. The atmosphere at the stadium was electric as both sides looked to secure their progression in a competition that has become a vital battlefield for silverware. A Dream Start and VAR Drama The match ignited within the opening sixty seconds. Arsenal wasted no time establishing dominance as Riccardo Calafiori found the back of the net with a clinical left-footed finish, following a sharp assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly . The goal was briefly held in the balance during a tense VAR review, but the referee eventually pointed to the center spot, confirming the lead. Manchester City struggled to find their rhythm early on, evidenced by Phil Foden receiving a yellow card for unsportsmanlike conduct as frustrations began to simmer. As the first half progressed, the visitors' tactical discipline kept the hosts at bay. The City midfield, usually so dominant in possession, found itself crowded out by a hungry Arsenal press that refused to let the game settle into a predictable pattern. Clinical Execution and Goal-Line Clearances The Gunners doubled their advantage in the 28th minute through a beautifully orchestrated team move. Martin Ødegaard provided the vision with a key pass to Christos Tzolis , who delivered a perfect cross for Kai Havertz to head home. The drama intensified ten minutes later when Riccardo Calafiori was booked for diving in the penalty box—a controversial decision that denied Arsenal a chance for a third from the spot. Late in the first half, both ends of the pitch saw incredible defensive heroics. Martin Ødegaard saw a certain goal hacked off the line, only for Jeremy Doku to experience the same frustration at the other end moments later. These narrow escapes kept the scoreline at 2-0 heading into the interval, leaving the door slightly ajar for a potential comeback. Ødegaard Seals the Deal Any hopes of a Manchester City recovery were effectively extinguished just three minutes after the restart. Martin Ødegaard , who had been the architect of so much of his team's success, turned scorer by finishing with his left foot after excellent work from Tzolis and Lewis-Skelly . The 3-0 deficit prompted Pep Guardiola to make sweeping changes, including replacing Erling Haaland with Omar Marmoush , but the momentum remained firmly with the North Londoners. Despite late pressure from Antoine Semenyo and creative sparks from Rayan Cherki , the Arsenal defense remained resolute. Gabriel and Piero Hincapie made crucial interventions to protect the clean sheet. In front of a crowd of 58,056 , the final whistle confirmed a comprehensive and deserved victory for the Gunners, as they marched into the next round with a performance of genuine authority.
